- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 3–5 days.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% over 30d), check sentiment for bullish bias — if sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 5–10% to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment is positive and model is below true outcome, consider slight upward bias correction — but only if recent price is trending upward; avoid overcorrection.
- Model often underestimates true price in early 30d horizon when sentiment is volatile — add 1–2% to forecast if sentiment swings >0.15 in last 5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive and price is trending downward, model may lag — adjust forecast to reflect recent downward momentum by adding 1–3% to forecast for next 5 days.
